entry.name: Deep Learning Specialization
entry.note: Five courses from dense networks through sequence models; the standard second step

covers: Foundations of deep learning and neural networks
Convolutional neural networks for computer vision
Sequence models, RNNs, LSTMs and attention
Transformers and natural language processing with word embeddings
Hyperparameter tuning, initialization, regularization and batch normalization
Diagnosing bias and variance and applying optimization algorithms
Running a machine learning project and prioritizing fixes
Implementing models in Python and TensorFlow
reading.format: Five courses delivered online. The page lists quizzes, ungraded labs and hands-on implementation work in Python and TensorFlow, including tasks such as visual detection and recognition, neural style transfer and character-level language modeling.
reading.summary: The Deep Learning Specialization is a five-course online program from DeepLearning.AI, created and taught by Andrew Ng. It starts with the basics of how neural networks work and moves through building and training them, then on to the techniques that improve their performance. Learners work with convolutional networks for vision tasks and sequence models for language, using Python and TensorFlow. One course covers running a machine learning project, including finding errors in a system and deciding what to fix first.
reading.audience: The page says it suits anyone wanting a thorough grounding in deep learning rather than a brief overview. It names software engineers moving into AI, data scientists who want to understand what happens under the hood, and early-career or aspiring machine learning engineers building a portfolio.
reading.prerequisites: Comfort with Python and basic linear algebra. Prior machine learning experience is helpful but not required.
